newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece drafts bill setting up derivatives market.
newsitem.headline: Greece drafts bill setting up derivatives market.

text.p: Greece on Tuesday set out a long-awaited draft bill to help investors hedge against risk by creating a derivatives market.
"The bill on derivatives and other equity market regulations constitutes a major reform in the capital and money markets," national economy minister Yiannos Papandoniou told a news conference.

The prime goal of the bill is to create a derivatives exchange and a formal set of rules for their trade, he said. It also introduces reforms in the capital and money markets to promote transparency and the even distribution of information.
"Legislation is aimed at supervising and safeguarding all dealing in derivative products which, at an increasing rate, are traded off a formal bourse," Papandoniou said.
The Athens stock exchange will participate in the share capital of the derivatives bourse and the associated clearing house along with other institutional market participants.
The bill also deals with the exchange's guarantee fund which, at its current state, is considered inadequate to cope with present trading volumes and operating requirements.

With the consent of participating Greek brokers, broad reforms shall include tripling the fund's assets, linking contributions of members to transaction volumes, compliance with EU directives on investor protection and overhauling investor compensation procedures.
Transparency and even distribution of information will be improved by requiring listed companies to post quarterly financial statements within two months following each quarter.

The bill will also introduce tougher surveillance of deals in equity-linked instruments by board members and large shareholders of listed companies, brokerages and institutional investors as well as financial journalists.
The capital market commission will be required to report to the government and the parliament on an annual basis on its activities and operations.
The roll-back of the state from the Athens stock exchange will be pursued by means of an expansion of its capital base among Greece's brokers, credit institutions and other institutional investors.
Papandoniou did not say when the bill would be submitted to parliament, where it may undergo changes before it is approved by vote. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
